[{:db/id 17592186198378 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-22bda1b7-731c-5be9-8f1b-6668d9e068b6"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-22bda1b7-731c-5be9-8f1b-6668d9e068b6" :question/id #uuid "22bda1b7-731c-5be9-8f1b-6668d9e068b6" :question/math-academy-id "q-161253" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,xz,\,yz⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{u}^{2},\,v⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}auv+b{u}^{2}v\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2u & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,-1,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,xz,\,yz⟩{|}_{x=u\,y={u}^{2}\,z=v} \\  & =⟨v,\,uv,\,{u}^{2}v⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨v,\,uv,\,{u}^{2}v⟩\cdot ⟨2u,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =v\cdot 2u+uv\cdot (-1)+{u}^{2}v\cdot 0 \\  & =2uv-uv+0 \\  & =uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1\cdot uv+0\cdot {u}^{2}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=1+0=1.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-c1855324-ee18-529c-ba15-53c93565cb17"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,xz,\,yz⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{u}^{2},\,v⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}auv+b{u}^{2}v\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$"] ["question-22bda1b7-731c-5be9-8f1b-6668d9e068b6" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2u,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 2u & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,-1,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,xz,\,yz⟩{|}_{x=u\,y={u}^{2}\,z=v} \\  & =⟨v,\,uv,\,{u}^{2}v⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨v,\,uv,\,{u}^{2}v⟩\cdot ⟨2u,\,-1,\,0⟩ \\  & =v\cdot 2u+uv\cdot (-1)+{u}^{2}v\cdot 0 \\  & =2uv-uv+0 \\  & =uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1\cdot uv+0\cdot {u}^{2}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=1+0=1.
$$"] ["question-22bda1b7-731c-5be9-8f1b-6668d9e068b6" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-c1855324-ee18-529c-ba15-53c93565cb17" :answer-field/id #uuid $$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨x,\,y,\,-z⟩|}_{x=u+v\,y=v-u\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u+v,\,v-u,\,-uv⟩\cdot ⟨-u-v,\,v-u,\,2⟩ \\  & =(u+v)\cdot (-u-v)+(v-u)\cdot (v-u)+(-uv)\cdot 2 \\  & =-{u}^{2}-2uv-{v}^{2}+{v}^{2}-2uv+{u}^{2}-2uv \\  & =-6uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$

17592186045485 :db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨-{u}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.$*" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=-{u}^{2}\,y=2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2(-{u}^{2})+(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,2({v}^{2}),\,(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =(-{v}^{2})\cdot 8uv+2{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv+2{u}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =-8u{v}^{3}+8u{v}^{3}+8{u}^{3}v \\  & =8{u}^{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{u}^{3}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}

respect to the unit normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ is given by 

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf F \cdot \textrm{d} \mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S  \mathbf F \cdot {\color{blue}\mathbf{n}} \,\textrm{d}S,
$$

where ${\color{blue}\mathbf{n}}$ is a unit normal vector that defines the orientation of the surface.

![](images/9a/9aa63a1e4f1d278cef6c53600e8fb9c60829de972ba7409afdc32837ecbc3e07.png)

If $S$ is given by a parametric equation of the form 

$$
\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{r}(u,v), \qquad (u,v)\in D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,
$$

we can determine the unit normal vector using the fundamental product as follows:

$$
{\color{blue}\mathbf{n}} = \dfrac{\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v}{\| \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \|}
$$

 

Substituting this into the formula for the flux, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot \frac{{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}}{‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot \frac{{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}}{‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖}\,‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $S$ is a smooth, orientable surface given in parametric form by $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,$ then the flux of the vector field $\mathbf{F}$ across $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf F \cdot \textrm{d} \mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_D  \mathbf F(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \: \textrm{d}A.
$$
